core.title: Bind the plan decomposition to a local issue record before the plan is locked
core.given: A plan session holds a decomposition of the work into plan artifacts. It may have started with no pre-existing issue record or brief.
core.when: You lock (confirm/ratify) the decomposition and author the plan artifacts.
core.then: Before the lock, bind the decomposition to a local issue record — an existing target issue's local identifier, or one minted from the main job — and author the plan as that issue's plan-phase artifacts on its registered branch and worktree.
prefer: Start conversationally and decompose before any issue paperwork; no pre-existing issue record or brief is needed. Bind any time before the lock.
Bind the open session to an existing local issue record — list the bindable records, or mint one from the main job.
Bind by the local issue record's identifier; a remote issue tracker's number is a synced projection added later.
avoid: Reading 'no up-front ceremony' as 'no issue at all'. The session removes the ceremony, not the issue.
Locking an unbound decomposition, or authoring plan artifacts on an untracked branch (no issue + registered branch + worktree).
Waiting for, or binding by, a remote issue tracker's issue number.
core.why: The rule that every repository modification needs an issue + registered branch + worktree must always hold, even with no remote issue tracker, so plan artifacts always land on a tracked branch tied to a local issue record.
evidence: Attempting to lock (confirm) a decomposition with no bound issue is refused.
Plan artifacts are authored on the bound issue's registered branch and worktree as that issue's plan-phase artifacts.
verification: Enforced at the session's lock step: the lock (confirm) operation must refuse to lock a decomposition that is not bound to an issue, so plan artifacts are never authored on an untracked branch.
The binding identity the check accepts is the local issue record's identifier, not a remote issue tracker's number; the tracker is a downstream integration whose numbers are synced projections.
Out of scope: starting or running a session with no pre-existing issue record or brief — that is allowed; only the lock requires a binding.

values: confirm attempted with no issue bound
plan artifacts authored on a branch with no registered issue/worktree

fires: The planner starts a plan session with no pre-existing issue record or brief (allowed; binding is required only before the lock).
The planner binds an issue to an open session (an existing local issue record, or one minted from the main job).
The planner is about to lock (confirm/ratify) a decomposition, bound or not.
The planner authors plan artifacts after the plan is locked.
doesNotFire: Work unrelated to a plan session (e.g. implementation changes on an already-planned issue).

neutralityNotes: The obligation is process-level, so the core needs almost no structural profile data; the single profile requirement says which artifact kinds count as plan artifacts (roles.plan_artifact.kinds). The local issue record store (manifest/State Store) and the remote tracker (GitHub, with its synced number) have no vocabulary key, but the core states the obligation without them — it keeps 'local issue record' vs 'remote issue-tracker projection' abstract and leaves the concrete identities in bunOnly — so no key was proposed. Branch and worktree are VCS-level concepts and were kept as-is. 'plan session', 'ratify', 'PLANNED' and the issue + branch + worktree iron rule are treated as methodology-level (ATDD process) terms rather than stack specifics; each realization supplies its own operation spellings (see bunOnly for activation.facts[0], prefer[1]). Per-rule severity and disposition stay in core:verification.
